name: Twin red stripes (1985)
description: TWA's scheme from the mid-1970s, as worn in 1985: an all-white body with two red stripes along it just under the cabin windows, separated by a thin white line. Both start thin at the nose and widen downward toward the tail, the upper one's top edge level along the windows (on the 747 right against them). On the widebodies the lower stripe's bottom edge reaches the belly behind the wing, so the aft lower body is red to the tail cone. 'TRANS WORLD' in red bold italic capitals over the forward windows. On the white fin a broad red band runs across from just behind the leading edge to just ahead of the trailing edge, its front and back edges parallel to the fin's, with 'TWA' in heavy white italic capitals on it. Bare metal engine cowlings, gray wings, a black anti-glare panel round the windshield.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on 727-200 N64339 (June 1985, fitted to shapes/B722.json), with the MD-80, L-1011 and 747 as types. The scheme dates from about 1975 and lasted, with small changes, into the mid-1990s (both dates approximate). Every edge is a fitted line, not a trace: each stripe edge is one straight line in meters from the nose to the tail (within 0.05 m of the photo's along the cabin; nearer the nose and on the tail cone, where the photos' curvature and shadow made the stripes seem to rise, they're kept straight, as paint lines laid out on the side elevation), sampled at the body profile's own points so it draws straight; the fin band's front and back edges are straight lines parallel to the fin's. The white line between the stripes is about 0.1 m and holds its height while the stripes widen away from it. On the 727 and the L-1011 the band runs down past the fin's root over the center engine's fairing; the renderer carries the fin's paint there to the fairing's foot, so it reaches the body where on the aircraft it stops a little above it (0.5-1 m of white). 'TWA' on the 727 sits low on the band, mostly over the S-duct's fairing. The registration (red, on the S-duct by the flag) isn't drawn. Reds on the photos range from brick to crimson with the film; the palette's red is a middle reading, not TWA's specification. Refitted 2026-11-24 on the passenger 727 (shapes/B722-passenger.json, with its windows): measured against N64339's windows and forward door, the stripes were about 0.43 m low and the title on the window row; both raised (the stripes' straight edges kept, the cabin made level), the title's baseline now 0.39 m over the windows' middle and its capitals 0.44 m.

MD82.note: The MD-80's stripes start at the radome's joint about 1.2 m back and run straight to the tail, widening as on the 727 (the upper one downward, the lower one more so); the lower one runs off the belly under the tail cone. White nacelles with a bare metal lip. On the fin the red band runs from the root to just over half way up, its front corners rounded, with 'TWA' nearly filling it. Measured on MD-82 N914TW (left side, July 1985) fitted to shapes/MD82.json; the fin's band and lettering as shares of the fin's own outline in the photo, as the fit couldn't match the body and the fin together. The stripes' edges are straight lines in meters, nose to tail (within 0.05 m of the photo's along the cabin).

L101.note: On the TriStar the stripes start at the nose and widen downward along its longer body. Re-measured 2026-11-25 on N31001 (left) and the right-side photo (July 1984) against the windows and doors: unlike the 747's the upper stripe doesn't touch the windows, a white gap about 0.22 m deep holds all along (its top edge level at z 0.05 m, the windows' bottom 0.27 m; it had fallen to 0.57 m below them aft). Its lower edge -0.057 m at the nose falling 0.0213 m per meter, a white line 0.13-0.2 m, the lower stripe's top -0.19 m falling 0.024 per meter and its bottom -0.279 m falling 0.0482 per meter, which meets the belly 42.6 m back, behind the wing: aft of it the lower body is red to the tail cone (the bottom edge read only to 14 m ahead of the wing and at 35-43 m in the wing's shadow, where the photo's red stops about 2.2 m under the centerline above the white belly). Each edge a straight line in meters, a point at each of the shape's crown and belly points, within 0.3 mm. (Before, from the 2026-11-24 fit: the stripes ran about 0.3 m low behind door 2.) On the fin the red band runs from under a white tip (with the flag) down past the fin's root over the center engine's intake fairing, its front edge parallel to the leading edge with a white margin and its back edge near the trailing edge. 'L-1011' in red on the intake's fairing. Measured on L-1011-1 N31001 (left side, August 1984) fitted to shapes/L101.json within 6 px. Over the intake the renderer carries the fin's band down to the fairing's foot, where on the aircraft it stops about 0.8 m above the body (docs/COORDINATES.md: a tail engine's paint).

B742.note: On the 747-100 and -200 (shapes/B742.json): measured 2026-11-25 on the side-on 747-131 (January 1985, right side, flipped) against the main deck's windows and the five doors, each edge a straight line in meters from the nose to where it meets the outline. The upper stripe's top edge runs right along the bottom of the main deck's windows (z -0.26 m, the windows' -0.262), touching them, from the nose to the tail cone. Its lower edge falls from -0.34 m at the nose by 0.0302 m per meter (-0.94 m by door 2, -1.57 m by door 4). A white line 0.21 m deep runs under it, and under that the thinner lower stripe, its bottom edge from -0.67 m at the nose falling 0.0582 m per meter (-1.75 m by door 2). That edge is steeper than the belly's, so it meets the belly 45.9 m back, just behind the wing: aft of it the red runs down to the belly, and from about door 4 back the body under the white line is red to the tail (red in the photo's shadow there, where the white belly ahead of the wing reads gray). The white line meets the belly at 52.2-53.1 m, ahead of door 5, and from there the red is one broad band from the windows' height to the belly. It ends where the windows' height meets the tail cone's underside, 60.8 m back. Within about 0.05 m of the photo along the cabin forward of the wing and 0.1 m behind it (the wing hides 22-41 m). Checked on the left side (October 1984, taking off): the same stripe against the windows and the same red aft lower body. The title re-measured on the side-on photo by doors 1 and 2: 8.5 to 21.1 m back, capitals 0.88 m tall on a baseline 1.22 m above the centerline, under the upper deck's three windows. On the fin the red band runs from just above the root to a white tip, its front edge parallel to the leading edge with a white margin. Each stripe edge has a point at each of the shape's crown and belly points along it, more where needed to draw within 0.3 mm.
